label: TP
reason: User input from HTTP header flows directly into the XML/XPath expression via concatenation without proper filtering. Although ESAPI.encodeForHTML is used in the error message handler, it is applied only to the variable in the catch block, not to the 'bar' variable used in the XPath expression at line 70. The XPath sink receives unfiltered user input, allowing potential injection attacks.

evidence.note: User input retrieved from header and decoded.
Input passed to doSomething which returns it unchanged.
Unsanitized bar variable concatenated into XPath expression.
ESAPI encoder used only in exception handler, not protecting the main execution path.
